questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the headlights of oncoming cars. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT safe on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic must keep to the right.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you move left or right. Keep to the right lane if you are slower than other traffic. If you miss your exit, go to the next one. You cannot back up or make a U-turn on the interstate.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection. When turning on a green light, always yield to pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area ahead.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs are used for construction and maintenance areas.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line in the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines mean any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates or disabled parking placards.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal blood alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment is needed to react properly while driving. Even below the legal limit, any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line, what can you do?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They alert inattentive drivers with vibration and sound when their vehicle leaves the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert inattentive drivers with vibration and sound when their vehicle leaves the lane.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam.
Use high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when other cars are not nearby. Use low beams when following closely behind another driver.

questions.question: Should you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: Yes, if the car ahead is turning left.
No, never.
Yes, if the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never pass another vehicle on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you to be there and may pull off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells drivers that roadwork is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic control devices in work zones.

questions.question: How do sudden wind gusts affect vehicles on highways?

options.text: They only affect large vehicles.
They only cause visibility problems.
They can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dirt and dust onto the road. It can also physically push a vehicle.

questions.question: Why use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, headlights make your vehicle easier to see. If you need to use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road ahead has curves and turns.
Traffic increases ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that the road is slippery when wet and to reduce speed.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly during heavy traffic or bad weather. However, do not drive so slowly that you block the normal flow of traffic. You can be ticketed for this.

questions.question: What should you do if a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle?

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to have complete control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable. Young riders often make sudden changes in direction. Remember that children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed with caution.

questions.question: The light is green, but traffic blocks the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait until traffic clears before entering.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until traffic clears before entering.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic blocks your way, even with a green light. If you get stuck in the intersection when the light turns red, you will block other traffic and can get a ticket.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn after coming to a complete stop.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means do not proceed in that direction. Come to a full stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: Your vehicle will not fit completely across the tracks on the other side.
The crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
You are carrying two or more young children in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle will not fit completely across the tracks on the other side.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time, from either direction. Do not start crossing unless your vehicle can completely clear the tracks. Never stop your vehicle on the tracks.

questions.question: "BAC" means:

options.text: Blood alcohol concentration.
Big alcohol content.
Blood alcohol conservation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. Drivers 21 and older are considered impaired when their BAC is 0.08 percent or higher.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
Other drivers when they want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not cut in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reactions slow and unreliable.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows all body functions and nerve responses. It reduces your control and makes it harder to concentrate and stay alert.
